## The puzzle

```{=html}
<div class="concise-only">
```

Khamenei was killed in the opening hours of 28 February 2026. Decapitation typically compels concession — a regime's leadership is taken off the board and the survivors settle. In January 2020 Trump killed Soleimani; Iran fired symbolic missiles at US Iraqi bases and de-escalated within a week. In February 2026 Trump killed the Supreme Leader; ten weeks later Iran is still in the fight, the IRGC has consolidated, the renminbi-toll regime is operational, and the dual blockade continues. Same US administration, opposite outcome. Why?

```{=html}
</div>
<div class="deep-only">
```

On the night of 27-28 February 2026, coordinated US-Israeli strikes hit Iranian nuclear and command infrastructure. In the opening hours, Ali Khamenei — Iran's Supreme Leader since 1989 — was killed. Decapitation strikes are typically expected to compel concession: the regime's defining figure is taken off the board, the institutional successors face an existential moment of weakness, and they settle quickly to consolidate. Iran's *previous* exposure to a Trump decapitation strike fit this pattern. In January 2020, Qasem Soleimani — IRGC Quds Force commander, operationally critical but institutionally replaceable — was killed in a US strike at Baghdad airport. Iran responded with symbolic missile strikes on US bases in Iraq, deliberately calibrated to avoid US casualties, and de-escalated within a week. The Qaani succession installed without regime crisis. The 2020 case looks like a textbook decapitation-compels-concession outcome. The 2026 case looks like the opposite: IRGC consolidation under Vahidi (de facto leadership), sustained war prosecution, refusal to settle, renminbi-toll alternative architecture operationalized, dual blockade continuing through 8 May 2026. Same US administration in both cases. The variable is the strike target's role. The puzzle Q2 sets: *why has the war persisted past initial strikes — particularly after successful Iranian decapitation that should, on the standard model, have compelled concession?*

Khamenei's death triggered IRGC institutional gamble-for-resurrection; Vahidi (de facto leadership) faces existential stake; no acceptable concession exists that preserves the IRGC's institutional position. Operates through (i) decision-making sidelining of Pezeshkian, (ii) "survival = victory" framing internalized via Weeks-style observability/value-of-backing-down channels, (iii) alternative-architecture construction (renminbi-toll) as defensive regime-survival response. **β — US-side [audience-cost lock-in]{.gloss data-gloss="audience-costs-fearon"} via Putnam + Fearon + [Q10's α producer-coalition dominance]{.gloss data-gloss="grossman-helpman-lobby"}** (P operative 0.75; P load-bearing 0.55). Trump-admin war-aim expansion (preventive defense → regime change → oil seizure) is a Putnam Level-II lock-in; each public escalation increases the cost of backing down without visible result; reinforced by Q10's producer-coalition lobby weight. **γ — Structural commitment-trap envelope** (P operative 0.95; P load-bearing 0.50): [Walter 1997 no-third-party-enforcer]{.gloss data-gloss="walter-third-party-enforcement"} + [Werner 1999 all-three-diagnostics-fail]{.gloss data-gloss="werner-peace-durability"} + Powell-Reiter mutual commitment failure + [Pape coercion-failure]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-coercion"} + Schelling commitment-irreversibility (Khamenei assassination forecloses Iranian face-saving exit). Critical META rule 3 distinction: *retrospective* persistence (why HAS it persisted to 8 May 2026) is high-confidence at P ≈ 0.70; *prospective* persistence (will it continue) is admin-contingent at P ≈ 0.55, because β is Q10-admin-contingent — if Trump pivots under gasoline-price stress, β collapses, and α alone cannot sustain war without US prosecution.

## Methodology — Tier-2 abbreviated protocol + the four-fold validated principled-multi-framework pattern

This chapter applies the Tier-2 abbreviated protocol: pre-Q corpus audit, four new corpus acquisitions (Walter 1997, Fortna 2003, Werner 1999 compilation, Stedman 1997), steel-mans A/B/C written in-house, the seven META rules applied throughout. The candidate mechanism set reduced from nine to three via the META rule 4 discipline, with an in-analysis correction reassigning the renminbi-toll mechanism from β to α-side. Q2 is the fourth principled-multi-framework case in the project (after Q7, Q9, Q10) — the pattern is well-validated. The Soleimani-Khamenei base-rate test is the most distinctive analytical contribution available and would have been very hard to surface without the META rule 2 discipline. The retrospective-vs-prospective distinction (META rule 3 applied per mechanism, not globally) is structurally cleaner than Q10's full admin-contingency: Q2 has structurally-locked-in components (α + γ) that persist even if β collapses, but the war itself ends if β collapses because war requires US participation.
:::

**The [Soleimani-Khamenei differential]{.gloss data-gloss="soleimani-khamenei-differential"} is Q2's load-bearing base-rate test (META rule 2 application).** Two strike outcomes six years apart, with the same US administration (Trump, in both cases Republican president), the same Iranian state, and the same general policy posture. *January 2020 — Qasem Soleimani*: IRGC Quds Force commander, the operational head of Iran's regional proxy network. Killed by US drone strike at Baghdad airport. Operationally critical but institutionally replaceable — Qaani was installed without regime crisis. Iran's response: symbolic strikes on US bases in Iraq (Al Asad and Erbil), explicitly calibrated to avoid US casualties; de-escalation within a week; the standoff did not escalate to war. *February 2026 — Ali Khamenei*: Supreme Leader since 1989, the regime-defining figure. Killed in opening-hour strikes on a fortified bunker. Succession unresolved (Mojtaba Khamenei "behind security cordon" per ICG Crisis Monitor #4); IRGC institutional position existential. Iran's response: IRGC consolidation under Vahidi; sustained war prosecution; refusal to settle; renminbi-toll alternative architecture operationalized; dual blockade through 8 May 2026 and counting. The differential is what allows Q2 to identify the load-bearing mechanism: holding admin and target state constant, the variable is the *regime-defining-ness* of the struck leader. Goemans's framework predicts gamble-for-resurrection scales with the leader's institutional centrality; the differential empirically supports the prediction.

::: {.deep-only}
**Mechanism α — Iran-side regime-survival under [Goemans gamble-for-resurrection]{.gloss data-gloss="goemans-gamble-resurrection"} + [Weeks autocratic audience costs]{.gloss data-gloss="weeks-autocratic"}** (P operative 0.90; P load-bearing 0.65). The framework combination: Goemans 2000 — mixed-regime leaders facing severe personal punishment from defeat engage in gamble-for-resurrection, preferring escalation to settlement and hoping for low-probability turnaround. Weeks 2008 — autocratic audience costs operate via three channels: coordination among insiders, value-of-leader's-backing-down, observability of leader's commitment by domestic security-sector audience. The Q2 application: IRGC institutional position is existential. Khamenei's death triggered succession crisis (Mojtaba "behind security cordon"; succession unresolved per ICG Crisis Monitor #4). Vahidi as de facto leadership faces personal + institutional punishment-from-defeat threshold higher than Putin's per the Q7 application — defeat means the dismantling of IRGC's structural autonomy from the Iranian formal state, the institutional position the IRGC has built since 1979. Weeks-style audience costs: the IRGC security-sector audience values resistance commitment; backing down imposes high cost on Vahidi personally and on the IRGC institutionally. The renminbi-toll alternative-architecture construction is the regime-survival response — by building a non-dollar settlement option (China-financed Iran trade), Iran reduces dependence on a settlement that requires US concession. This is a *defensive structural move*, not an offensive war aim. The "survival = victory" framing visible in IRGC and Iranian official discourse is the cognitive surface of the Goemans + Weeks combined logic: Iran wins by surviving because the alternative (regime collapse) is catastrophic for IRGC leadership. Per META rule 3, α is *structurally-locked-in for the war's duration* — IRGC institutional consolidation is stable on multi-year horizon; the Goemans logic persists across leader-cycles (Vahidi → successor will face the same stakes); Mojtaba Khamenei succession, when it occurs, will not change α-mechanism because he is an IRGC-figurehead within the same institutional structure.

**Mechanism β — US-side audience-cost lock-in via Putnam + Fearon 1994 + [Q10's α producer-coalition dominance]{.gloss data-gloss="grossman-helpman-lobby"}** (P operative 0.75; P load-bearing 0.55, capped per Q10 admin-contingency). The framework combination: Putnam 1988 two-level games — admin's revealed policy is constrained by Level-II (domestic) win-set; Fearon 1994 — [audience costs make commitment credible]{.gloss data-gloss="audience-costs-fearon"} but also trap leaders past the backdown threshold; Q10's α-mechanism — Grossman-Helpman 1994 government objective function with low α-weight on aggregate consumer welfare under Trump admin specifically. The Q2 application: Trump's war-aim expansion (preventive defense → regime change → oil seizure → "no longer cared about negotiations") is a sequential public-commitment escalation. Each escalation tightens the Level-II constraint by enlarging the set of voters who would view backing-down-without-result as failure. Q10's α-mechanism reinforces β — producer-coalition rewards sustained disruption + LNG-export ramp; the consumer-coalition has not yet mobilized to the gasoline-price threshold (~$4.50/gal sustained 60 days per Q10) that would force pivot. Joint effect: Trump-admin sustained war prosecution is *doubly locked-in* (audience-cost + producer-coalition lobby weight). Per META rule 3, β is *currently-dominant under Trump admin but NOT structurally-locked-in across admins* — admin-change can reset (Q10's 2022 Biden base-rate established this); Q10 falsifier 2 (SPR acceleration > 5 mb/week sustained) is also Q2's β-falsifier; if Trump pivots, β collapses. This is the dimension that makes Q2 *prospective* persistence admin-contingent.

[**γ — Structural commitment-trap envelope.** [Walter 1997 third-party enforcement absent]{.gloss data-gloss="walter-third-party-enforcement"} + [Werner 1999 all three diagnostics fail]{.gloss data-gloss="werner-peace-durability"} (issues unresolved + enforcement absent + balance-of-power inconsistent) + Powell-Reiter mutual commitment failure + [Pape coercion-failure]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-coercion"} (US punishment cannot deny Iran's strategic options) + Schelling commitment-irreversibility (Khamenei assassination forecloses face-saving Iranian exit). Structurally-locked-in.]{.concise-only}

::: {.deep-only}
**Mechanism γ — Structural commitment-trap envelope** (P operative 0.95; P load-bearing 0.50). Six mutually-reinforcing framework components, none alone sufficient, jointly binding. *[Walter 1997]{.gloss data-gloss="walter-third-party-enforcement"}*: civil-war settlements require third-party security guarantee for credible commitment. The argument generalizes to interstate war termination where post-war compliance is at risk. The Q2 application: no third-party enforcer is available — Pakistan-mediated ceasefire lacks enforcement teeth; Pakistan cannot militarily compel compliance from either side; China + Russia vetoed UNSC enforcement resolution; Oman is too small to enforce. The result: settlement-via-mediation cannot produce stable peace; commitment problems persist permanently within current geopolitical configuration. *[Werner 1999]{.gloss data-gloss="werner-peace-durability"}*: post-war peace durable when (a) underlying issues resolved, (b) settlement includes enforcement, (c) terms consistent with balance of power. All three diagnostics fail simultaneously for the 2026 Iran-US case — *issues unresolved* (Iran's 14-point framework and US terms have no overlap on regime-change goal, enrichment access, Hormuz-toll regime); *enforcement absent* (Walter condition fails); *balance-of-power inconsistency* (terms acceptable to one side are inconsistent with the other side's revealed power-position — Iran cannot accept terms premised on its post-strike weakened position because Iran's revealed strategic options demonstrate continued bargaining power). *Powell-Reiter mutual commitment failure*: classic structure of unresolvable commitment problem; absolute victory is one solution but unachievable here. *[Pape coercion-failure]{.gloss data-gloss="pape-coercion"}*: punishment fails when target's strategic options are diverse and chokepoint-denial is feasible — exactly Iran's case (chokepoint denial; proxy network; alternative-architecture financial infrastructure). *Schelling commitment irreversibility*: Khamenei assassination is the ultimate irreversible commitment foreclosing face-saving Iranian de-escalation — Iran cannot "back down" without acknowledging defeat-of-regime-defining-figure's-death. *Slantchev 2011 costly signaling*: ongoing strikes signal commitment-resolve, raising audience-cost penalty for backing down. Per META rule 3, γ is *structurally-locked-in for the war's foreseeable duration* under current geopolitics — no third-party-enforcer mechanism is on the horizon; Werner diagnostics will continue to fail.
:::
:::

[**Reading the chart.** Each row is one of Q2's three load-bearing mechanisms. The light grey bar shows posterior P(operative) — how likely the mechanism is at play (all three are operative at 0.75-0.95). The colored foreground bar shows posterior P(load-bearing) — how much of the persistence the mechanism actually explains. The mechanisms are *jointly necessary* (α + β both required for war prosecution; γ required to prevent settlement), so their load-bearing weights are lower than their P(operative). α — Iran-side regime-survival — has the highest load-bearing weight (0.65) supported by the [Soleimani-Khamenei differential]{.gloss data-gloss="soleimani-khamenei-differential"} base-rate validation. β — US-side audience-cost lock-in — is capped at 0.55 by Q10's 2022 Biden base-rate disconfirmer (admin-contingent). γ — structural commitment-trap envelope — is at 0.50: highly operative (no third-party enforcer; Werner diagnostics all fail) but in the load-bearing sense the *envelope* is structural while individual war-prosecution mechanisms (α + β) are what produce active fighting.]{.deep-only}

[**META rule 3 applied per mechanism**, not globally. Retrospective Q2 (why HAS it persisted to 8 May) is high-confidence (P ≈ 0.70); all three mechanisms are operative and the war's continuation through May is fully explained. Prospective Q2 (will it continue) is admin-contingent (P ≈ 0.55) because β is reversible on admin change per Q10. If Trump pivots under gasoline-price stress, β collapses; α alone cannot sustain war without US prosecution; war could end via unilateral US exit.]{.concise-only}
[**The retrospective-vs-prospective distinction is structurally cleaner than Q10's full admin-contingency**. Q10's α-mechanism is fully admin-contingent; the strong-form claim was killed entirely by 2022 Biden. Q2's α-mechanism (Iran-side Goemans) is *structurally-locked-in* — IRGC institutional consolidation persists across leader-cycles. γ-mechanism (commitment-trap envelope) is *structurally-locked-in* — no third-party enforcer is on the horizon. Only β-mechanism (US-side audience-cost lock-in) is admin-contingent per Q10's finding. The result: Q2 retrospective persistence is high-confidence (P ≈ 0.70) — the joint α+β+γ explains the observed pattern through 8 May; Q2 prospective persistence is admin-contingent (P ≈ 0.55) — if Trump pivots to consumer-side, β collapses, and the war could end via unilateral US exit even though α and γ remain operative on the Iran side. This is a substantively different prediction from Q10's: under Q2, the war *might end* via β collapse, but Iran would still face all the structural drivers of regime-survival behavior; the post-war state would be unstable per Q3.]{.deep-only}

- **[T2]{.tier .tier-2} single-source named:** Goemans framework applies to IRGC institutional behavior (Goemans developed for state-level autocracies; IRGC is sub-state institution — mapping is inferential but consistent with Goemans's regime-survival logic); β reduces to admin-contingent rather than structural per Q10 base-rate (Q10 finding directly applies); [Walter 1997 third-party-enforcement]{.gloss data-gloss="walter-third-party-enforcement"} absence applies to Iran-US case (observable: Pakistan + Oman + China are not enforcement powers in Walter's sense).

- **[T3]{.tier .tier-3} inference from evidence:** **Vahidi specifically faces gamble-for-resurrection stake** (inferred from his institutional position + observable refusal-to-settle behavior); **the [Soleimani-Khamenei differential]{.gloss data-gloss="soleimani-khamenei-differential"} is explained by Goemans-stake variable** (cross-case inference; could equally support "Trump admin chose harder line in 2026" reading); **γ-envelope is jointly binding** (all 6-7 components mutually reinforce — theoretical convergence); **[Werner 1999 all-three-diagnostics-fail]{.gloss data-gloss="werner-peace-durability"}** (Werner's diagnostics derived from civil-war/COW dataset; interstate-war-with-asymmetric-stakes generalization is theoretical); **information-revelation has not yet converged bargaining ranges** (Hokayem "battle of endurance" framing; not directly measurable).

- **[T4]{.tier .tier-4} conjecture:** none in the load-bearing path.

**Five load-bearing T3 inferences** trigger the META rule 5 posterior cap at ≤ 0.65 on the multi-framework headline. The reconciled posterior sits at the cap.

## Pre-mortem {#pre-mortem}

The most likely ways the analysis will be wrong:

1. **Mistaken Vahidi-specific gamble-stake** (P ≈ 0.20). Vahidi is not in fact the de facto leader (alternative scenarios: Mojtaba Khamenei operating; council-led IRGC; Pezeshkian regaining authority). Mitigation: Goemans framework still applies to IRGC as institution even if specific actor identification differs.

2. **Information-revelation reading is correct** (P ≈ 0.20). The war is simply unfinished information-revelation (Wagner/Reiter) and will end via convergence rather than via mechanism α failure. Mitigation: information-revelation is folded into γ; principal framework remains multi-framework.

3. **Q10's β admin-contingency overstated** (P ≈ 0.20). Trump-admin producer-coalition dominance is more durable than 2022 Biden base-rate suggested (a 2028 Republican successor would pursue producer-side). Mitigation: doesn't change retrospective Q2 finding; prospective Q2 finding strengthens.

4. **Soleimani-Khamenei differential is confounded** (P ≈ 0.25). 2026 differs from 2020 along dimensions beyond strike-target-role (2024 Hezbollah/Hamas degradation lowered Iran's deterrent; Israel was different actor in 2026). Mitigation: even with confounders, the differential is consistent with Goemans prediction.

5. **Pakistan or Oman successfully constructs enforcement mechanism** (P ≈ 0.10). γ-envelope collapses. Mitigation: would require major-power-coalition realignment.

6. **Stedman spoilers framework should be a fourth mechanism** (P ≈ 0.15). IRGC and/or Netanyahu function as Stedman-type spoilers (total spoilers rejecting any agreement). Mitigation: spoiler dimension matters more for Q3 (post-ceasefire); Stedman applied here would be mechanism inflation.

**Total probability the finding is substantively wrong**: ≈ 0.35 (with overlap; not strictly additive). Consistent with the META-rule-5-capped posterior of 0.65.
